title: LASERSTONE: An Evidence-Aware and Provenance-Constrained Framework for the Scientific Evaluation of Natural Photonic Materials
domain: Natural photonic materials; scientific data provenance; computational evidence evaluation
research_question: Can heterogeneous photophysical evidence for natural photonic materials be integrated and evaluated without converting missing, semantically incompatible, or unit-ambiguous data into artificial numerical confidence or unsupported laser-performance claims?
scientific_gap: Photophysical databases and materials-informatics workflows support data access, calculation, harmonization, and provenance, but a domain-specific fail-closed mechanism is needed to determine whether each external photophysical quantity is scientifically compatible with a given downstream analysis and whether the resulting evidence authorizes a specific laser-related claim.
proposed_contribution: Evidence-state separation of literature-reported, derived, and missing quantities
Explicit semantic and unit contracts before cross-source mapping
Fail-closed handling of missing scientific quantities
Claim-level decision gating that separates evidence-supported analysis from unsupported laser-performance claims
Safe separation of isolated-compound evidence from plant-extract evidence
A unified external-evidence pipeline with provenance-preserving trace and output
evidence_scope: LASERSTONE G23 source code and automated tests
Three benchmark PhotochemCAD records: Asn-Bx, Quercetin, Lutein
Seven legacy LASERSTONE plant records for provenance audit
claim_boundary: Evidence-bounded computational validation only; no experimental laser action is claimed.
future_research_path: Scale to additional PhotochemCAD dye families
Perform experimental validation on selected candidates
Compare computational evidence readiness with laboratory measurements
